_: One measured run against a loaded district, committed so the prose in benchmarks/questions/*.cypher and docs/questions.md can be checked without an engine. Refresh with `python -m etl.probe_engine_capability --record`.

requires_edges.why: The prerequisite edges a loaded district holds. Quoted in tier 4 as 240.

courses.why: The district's courses. Quoted as 791 in five places.

chains_any_length.cypher: MATCH p = (:Course)-[:REQUIRES*]->(:Course) RETURN count(p) AS n
chains_any_length.why: Every prerequisite path. This is the 359 Q71 reported as cycles.

chains_length_two_or_more.cypher: MATCH p = (:Course)-[:REQUIRES*2..]->(:Course) RETURN count(p) AS n
chains_length_two_or_more.why: Paths long enough to have a cut vertex. Quoted in tier 4 and in Q68's note as 119 — a DIFFERENT figure from the one above, and named separately because reading them as one is how 119 and 359 end up in the same paragraph meaning the same thing.

deepest_chain.cypher: MATCH p = (:Course)-[:REQUIRES*]->(:Course) RETURN max(length(p)) AS n
deepest_chain.why: Q66's answer, and a bare aggregate — one row on any graph.

isolated_courses.cypher: MATCH (c:Course) WHERE NOT EXISTS { MATCH (c)-[:REQUIRES]->(:Course) } AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (:Course)-[:REQUIRES]->(c) } RETURN count(c) AS n
isolated_courses.why: Q67's answer. Typed as 431 in two files; the graph said 463.

repeated_variable_across_var_length.cypher: MATCH p = (c:Course)-[:REQUIRES*1..1]->(c) RETURN count(p) AS n
repeated_variable_across_var_length.why: Q71. Should be 0 — no course requires itself. The engine does not bind a repeated variable across a variable-length pattern, so it matches every edge instead.

in_over_a_node_list_from_a_separate_matc.cypher: MATCH p = (:Course)-[:REQUIRES*2..]->(:Course) MATCH (x:Course) WITH p, x WHERE x IN nodes(p) RETURN count(*) AS n
in_over_a_node_list_from_a_separate_matc.why: Q68's shape. Should be > 0 — some course is on some path. `x` comes from its own MATCH, and against a node list from elsewhere the test matches NOTHING.

not_in_over_a_node_list_from_a_separate_.cypher: MATCH p = (:Course)-[:REQUIRES*2..]->(:Course) MATCH (x:Course) WITH p, x WHERE NOT (x IN nodes(p)) RETURN count(*) AS n
not_in_over_a_node_list_from_a_separate_.why: The negation of the above. Should be very large. Also 0 — which is the finding: it matches nothing EITHER WAY rather than refusing, so Q68 answers "there are no articulation points" on a graph that has them.

in_over_a_node_list_unwound_from_the_pat.cypher: MATCH p = (:Course)-[:REQUIRES*]->(:Course) WITH p, nodes(p) AS ns UNWIND ns AS x WITH p, x WHERE x IN nodes(p) RETURN count(p) AS n
in_over_a_node_list_unwound_from_the_pat.why: The CONTRAST, and the reason the two above are recorded separately. Unwound from the path itself the same operator works. An earlier version of this probe measured only this shape, dropped `x` before the WHERE and recorded the scoping result as evidence about membership — which is the unchallengeable figure this probe exists against.

bare_single_node_map_absent_url.why: Should be 0. A bare single-node match does not apply its inline property map, so this counts the whole label.

relationship_pattern_map_absent_url.why: Should be 0, and IS — the same syntax inside a relationship pattern filters correctly. The contrast is the finding.

not_in_list_unparenthesised.cypher: MATCH (c:Course) WHERE NOT c.url IN ["a", "b"] RETURN count(c) AS n
not_in_list_unparenthesised.why: Should be every course. Without parentheses the membership test is not negated.

not_in_list_parenthesised.cypher: MATCH (c:Course) WHERE NOT (c.url IN ["a", "b"]) RETURN count(c) AS n
not_in_list_parenthesised.why: The same question written correctly, for the contrast.

bound_variable_in_property_map.cypher: MATCH (c:Course) WITH max(1) AS k MATCH (d:Course {district: k}) RETURN count(d) AS n
bound_variable_in_property_map.why: A bound variable inside a property map is a parse error, not a match.

aggregate_over_an_absent_label.cypher: MATCH p = (:NoSuchLabel)-[:REQUIRES*]->(:NoSuchLabel) RETURN max(length(p)) AS n
aggregate_over_an_absent_label.why: One row of null on a graph holding none of the label — which is why `records != []` is not an emptiness check.
